extracted.intended_audience: regulated firms and their counsel, petitioners and interested parties submitting or responding to Federal Register notices (food/pesticide/additive petitioners, quota holders, airlines, broadcasters), and federal agency staff implementing notices
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards appearing in Federal Register notices governing (a) duty-free quota administration, (b) filing/withdrawal/content of food-additive and pesticide petitions (including required specifications and analytical methods), (c) organizational functions of the National Library of Medicine, and (d) agency hearing/designation criteria (e.g., FCC, CAB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Show-cause triggers for quota cancellation or reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments may issue a show cause order when a firm has assembled watch units in a territory equal to or greater than 30 percent of its initial duty-free allocation, or whenever there is reason to believe shipments through Dec. 31, 1968 will be less than 80 percent of the number of units allocated to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon receipt of a show-cause order the firm has 30 days to show cause why its remaining quota should not be canceled or reduced; failure to show satisfactory cause permits cancellation or reduction as appropriate under the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure upon failure to show cause
rubrics_metrics.description: If a firm fails to show satisfactory cause why the remaining unused portion of its quota should not be canceled or reduced, that unused portion shall be either canceled or reduced, whichever is appropriate under the show-cause order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following cancellation or reduction, the Departments shall promptly reallocate the quota in a manner best suited to contribute to the economy of the islands among remaining firms; competitive bids from new firms may be invited if the Departments judge it appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual quota allocation formula (calendar year 1968)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual quotas will be allocated as soon as practicable after April 1, 1968 on the basis of: (1) the number of units assembled by each firm in the particular territory and entered duty-free into U.S. customs territory during 1967, and (2) the total dollar amount of wages subject to FICA taxes paid by the firm in the territory during 1967 attributable to its watch operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equal weight will be assigned to production/shipment history and wages subject to FICA taxes when making allocations under this formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data supply and verification requirement for allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: All data required must be supplied as a condition for allocations and are subject to verification by the Departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application forms will be mailed to recipients of initial quota allocations as soon as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of transfer-restriction rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules restricting transfers of duty-free quotas issued July 26, 1967 (published July 28, 1967) are incorporated by reference and apply to transfers of quotas issued during calendar year 1968.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to petition for amendment or repeal and to seek relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested party may petition for amendment or repeal of these rules and may seek relief from application of any provision upon a showing of good cause under the review procedures published Nov. 17, 1967.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief procedures follow the Secretaries of Commerce and the Interior's review procedures as previously published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of petitions procedure (food additives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions may be withdrawn without prejudice under 21 CFR 121.52 according to the procedural food additive regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices of withdrawal are published (example: Aquafine Corp. withdrew FAP 7M2150 proposing amendment to §121.3006).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of petitions procedure (pesticides)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions may be withdrawn without prejudice under 21 CFR 120.8 according to the pesticide regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices of withdrawal are published with citation to the withdrawn petition (examples provided for Chemagro Corp. and FMC Corp.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirement: proposed regulatory text and specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to amend a food-additive regulation must propose the amended regulatory text and provide a description of the additive and the changes to specifications (e.g., revised paragraphs (a) and (b) with descriptive text and specification values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: C. J. Patterson Co.'s petition proposed revised descriptive language and specified additive parameters such as acid number, calcium content, lactic acid content, and ester number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirement: proposed tolerances for pesticide residues
rubrics_metrics.description: Pesticide-related petitions must propose establishment of tolerances for residues (expressed in parts per million) on specified raw agricultural commodities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: petitions proposing tolerances of 10 ppm for apples/grapes/pears, 0.2 ppm for cottonseed/potatoes, 0.05 ppm for trifluralin on various commodities, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirement: proposed analytical methods for residue determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions proposing tolerances must include the analytical method(s) proposed for determining residues of the pesticide/herbicide/additive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include electron-capture gas chromatographic techniques, colorimetric techniques based on hydrolysis followed by measurement of complexes, microcoulometric GC with sulfur detection, gas chromatographic techniques, and multistep derivatization and colorimetric assays with absorbance readings (full method descriptions provided in notices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of conditions/limits of safe use in petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposing a food additive for a particular use (e.g., feed use), the petition must specify the proposed conditions or limits of use (e.g., ammoniated cottonseed meal as protein/nonprotein nitrogen source not to exceed 20 percent of total ration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation proposed should state the permissible uses and maximum percentages/conditions for safe use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical-method level of detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical methods described in petitions should be sufficiently detailed to permit evaluation, including sample extraction, clarification and cleanup steps, derivatization/hydrolysis if required, detection technique (GC, colorimetry), and measurement/readout (e.g., absorbance wavelength).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in notices include multi-step extraction + hydrolysis + diazotization + coupling to form a dye measured at specified millimicrons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency publication of petition notices and effective dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of filing or withdrawal of petitions are published in the Federal Register with filing and publication dates noted; regulatory changes and administrative orders include document numbers and filing timestamps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These published notices provide the official record of filing/withdrawal and procedural history.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Library of Medicine (NLM) mission and core functions
rubrics_metrics.description: NLM assists advancement of medical and related sciences through collection, dissemination, and exchange of information; serves as national medical information resource for federal and private entities; publishes/distributes guides, catalogs, and bibliographies; develops audiovisual materials; supports translation and publication of biomedical literature; supports medical library development and training; conducts research in recording/storing/retrieving/communicating health information; provides technical consultation and research assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of the Director, NLM: duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Directs and coordinates library activities; advises the Surgeon General on PHS policy relating to management and control of biomedical communication media; studies and defines needs in biomedical communications; provides secretariat for NLM Board of Regents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Public Information and Publications Management (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides information services for biomedical community and general public on NLM programs, coordinates publication and distribution of NLM publications via press releases, pamphlets, exhibits, and other media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Administrative Management (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides overall management and administrative services for the Library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Director for Research and Development (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducts R&D in biomedical communications and information sciences to improve communication of health information; applies technology to library operations and information systems; researches document/information handling networks, graphic image storage/retrieval/transmission, query languages and man-machine communication; applies operations research to NLM programs; evaluates ongoing systems and programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Computer and Engineering Services (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performs systems management of computer applications; systems analysis and design; computer programming support; operates and maintains digital computer and related data processing equipment; establishes production schedules and production control; produces and distributes magnetic tapes to MEDLARS centers and authorized users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Director for Extramural Programs (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administers grants and contracts to strengthen health sciences libraries and improve biomedical communications through nonfederal/private institutions; analyzes/evaluates extramural programs relative to objectives and national needs; provides grants management and administrative services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and Training Division functions (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports R&D projects to understand production/processing/communication patterns of biomedical information; identifies institutional and worker needs; applies knowledge to develop communication modalities; supports history of life sciences research; supports training projects to increase availability of medical librarians and communications specialists; awards traineeships/fellowships; makes special awards for comprehensive studies and critical literature reviews; provides secretariat services to advisory committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities and Resources Division functions (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administers grants for constructing/renovating/expanding health sciences libraries; augments basic resources; develops national system of regional medical libraries; provides secretariat services to advisory committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and Translations Division functions (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports preparation and publication of translations, indexes, bibliographies, abstracts and other publications to increase availability and utilization of published biomedical information; provides secretariat services to advisory committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Director for Library Operations (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administers Library’s direct operations; analyzes and evaluates operations against program needs; plans and administers a national biomedical library network.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Services Division functions (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommends policy on scope and coverage of the collection; acquires and catalogs materials; develops/maintains international publication exchange relationships; publishes catalogs of acquisitions and holdings; studies mechanization/automation of technical services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Services Division functions (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides reference services, administers interlibrary loan program, maintains/circulates/preserves collection, provides photographic and photocopying services, and operates a graphic image storage and retrieval program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic Services Division functions (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyzes and indexes medical literature for publication; prepares research bibliographies; prepares requests for special bibliographies for computer processing; develops recurring bibliographic services; develops/produces Index Medicus and related publications; maintains medical subject heading authority list.

rubrics_metrics.name: History of Medicine Division functions (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquires, organizes and services historical source materials; performs research in history of medicine; publishes catalogs, bibliographies and aids to medical-historical scholarship; collects and controls historical pictorial materials including films, prints, photographs, slides and paintings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Director for Specialized Information Services (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinates development/operation of specialized information services; plans, develops, and operates national toxicological information system; organizes/analyzes published information on effects of drugs and chemicals, preparing special bibliographies and reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of the Associate Director for Audiovisual-Telecommunications (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans, directs, coordinates and evaluates national biomedical audiovisual and telecommunications program; provides program management support for the National Medical Audiovisual Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Medical Audiovisual Center functions (NLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operates central facility for development, production, distribution, evaluation and utilization of motion pictures, videotapes and other audiovisual forms; coordinates audiovisual program to assure responsiveness and economy; provides consultation/assistance for specialized audiovisual activities; encourages production/dissemination/utilization of medical films and audiovisuals; operates national clearinghouse and archival program; acts as national/international film and videotape center for distribution/exchange of biomedical audiovisuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual exclusivity and interference standard (FCC hearing designation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are mutually exclusive where operation as proposed would result in mutually destructive interference; such mutually exclusive applications are subject to consolidated hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission considers mutual exclusivity and destructive interference as a ground to designate applications for hearing under section 309(e) of the Communications Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative standard metric: 1 mV/m contour population and service area
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of comparison among mutually exclusive FM proposals, the areas and populations within the 1 mV/m contours and availability of other FM services of 1 mV/m or greater intensity in those areas will be considered under the standard comparative issue to determine comparative preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data submitted should indicate differences in area/population served and availability of other services; the 1 mV/m contour is the standard geographic/population metric cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program duplication admissibility and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposals differ materially in the amount of AM programming duplicated, evidence regarding program duplication will be admissible under the standard comparative issue; if duplicated programming is proposed, the showing permitted will be limited to evidence concerning benefits to be derived from the proposed duplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full comparison of applicants' program proposals will not be permitted in the absence of a specific programming inquiry (citing Jones v. Sudbury precedent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory finding issue for comparative hearings (FCC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated hearing issues include: (1) which proposal would best serve the public interest, and (2) in light of evidence, which application for a construction permit should be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are to present evidence on these issues at the consolidated hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appearance filing requirement for hearing (FCC §1.221(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must, within twenty (20) days of mailing of the order, file in triplicate a written appearance stating intention to appear and present evidence, in person or by attorney, pursuant to §1.221(c) of Commission rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file the written appearance within the time prescribed may forfeit opportunity to be heard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing publication requirement (FCC §1.594 and sec. 311(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must give notice of the hearing either individually or jointly within the time and manner prescribed by §1.594 of the rules, and must advise the Commission of publication of such notice as required by §1.594(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must comply with the Communications Act and the Commission’s publication rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB) conditional approval and petition-for-review period
rubrics_metrics.description: CAB approved an agreement (CAB 19654, R-49 through R-64) provided approval does not constitute approval of specific commodity descriptions for tariff publication; persons entitled may petition the Board for review pursuant to 14 CFR 385.50 within 10 days after service of the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order becomes effective upon expiration of the 10-day petition period unless petitioned or the Board reviews on its own motion; the order will be published in the Federal Register.
